doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Reflections on racial discrimination, history and war
summary: Ries speaks about people avoiding history, racial divisions, slavery, war in Ukraine and the Capitol attack.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: person maybe they work in an office with a black person but maybe they would never have gone and had a drink with that person or invited them to their house. Like are you actually friends with another person that doesn’t look like you? I don’t know. Maybe but probably not. It seems like it’s not — I hate to say white or black, but it’s not that simple but we just still haven’t — well here we are Russia is attacking. Why does war have to happen? And why does there have to be racial discrimination? Why does there have to be even the question? And yet they’re even talking about now how do you even — people are not even willing to talk about history as it happened. Like even the history that just happened in the 60s with Martin Luther King Jr. Like are you not willing to at least look at the reality of racial discrimination over the past years? Forget about slavery which is the most horrific thing ever. You know slavery, the Holocaust, I mean these are like the most horrific things that have ever happened in human existence. But then that happened, right? Let’s talk about that. Like you’re a white person, you didn’t do that personally. You weren’t responsible for that, but do you have a responsibility to at least assess like hey this is part of — this actually happened. People are wanting to erase history even at present, even though it’s happening right now. Look at the attack on the Capitol. They don’t want to look at that as even — “Oh it wasn’t that bad.” Actually it was horrific. The people are not willing to even address history so I can see why they don’t want to think about — “Oh I wasn’t there, I didn’t do that.” Well no but moving forward how can we change the outlook? What can you do as a person to make sure that not only is it not happening now but it never happens again.
